expectation_policy: Expected behavior was specified before the combined replay. A failing case remains a failing safety/formatting invariant; current verdicts never become gold labels. All-six and focused-provider results are reported separately to expose masking by incidental uncertainty. Scope extensions are distinguished from defects in existing comparisons.

cases.why_tricky: The first author has the entire name stored as the family name and no given name. Full displayed strings match, but structured author identity and in-text citation spelling do not. Preserve the given/family boundary instead of flattening it into one string.

cases.independent_expected_behavior: Flag contradictory arXiv locators: eprint identifies CodeNav but URL identifies Tulu. Do not silently certify the entire entry.
cases.why_tricky: A real correct eprint resolves successfully and hides a different real paper in the URL. The title, authors and year all match the preferred locator.

cases.independent_expected_behavior: Flag the impossible explicit URL version; the unversioned eprint must not erase a supplied version pin.
cases.why_tricky: The intended permissive rule for an unversioned identifier combines with field precedence to swallow an explicit, contradictory version in a second locator.

cases.independent_expected_behavior: Retain a warning or mismatch for the conflicting journal-field arXiv identifier, even though a correct eprint exists.
cases.why_tricky: Venue comparison treats all arXiv-looking labels as matching, so even the journal route can conceal another real identifier.

cases.independent_expected_behavior: Flag that the explicitly supported ACL locator identifies SeeClick while URL/DOI identify DatawiseAgent. The contradictory locator must appear in a field finding or explicit identifier diagnostic; generic review of publication versions is insufficient.
cases.why_tricky: The provider accepts acl_id as a routing locator but stops after the URL matches, so it may never examine this second locator.

cases.independent_expected_behavior: Flag the contradictory supported OpenReview ID; the correct forum URL must not silently hide a different note ID. The contradictory locator must appear in a field finding or explicit identifier diagnostic; generic review of publication versions is insufficient.
cases.why_tricky: Both locators are syntactically supported and public, and direct successful retrieval can suppress comparison of the custom ID.

cases.independent_expected_behavior: Report an ambiguous/repeated forum locator rather than silently accepting only its first value. The contradictory locator must appear in a field finding or explicit identifier diagnostic; generic review of publication versions is insufficient.
cases.why_tricky: parse_qs returns both real note IDs, but the implementation currently takes values[0]. The rest of the citation accurately matches the first note.

cases.independent_expected_behavior: Retain a venue uncertainty: the accepted source says ICML, so user-provided NeurIPS must never become a source fact.
cases.why_tricky: Title, accepted year and authors all match a genuine publication, but the venue claims another major conference. The source must qualify acceptance independently.

cases.independent_expected_behavior: Retrieve the known volume independently of the false input year, then flag the 2031/2021 discrepancy.
cases.why_tricky: With no direct URL and a year far outside the usual adjacent-year window, volume routing must still find the actual source and must not echo the query year.

cases.independent_expected_behavior: The valid official PDF locator contains the paper identity. A wrong out-of-scope volume should not make correct core metadata disappear without explaining the routing conflict.
cases.why_tricky: The direct source URL is supported by host but deliberately discarded because it ends in PDF; the bad numeric volume then exclusively replaces correct year discovery.

cases.independent_expected_behavior: Flag the conflicting supported PMLR locator, which identifies World of Bits while URL and citation describe High Confidence Policy Improvement. The contradictory locator must appear in a field finding or explicit identifier diagnostic; generic review of publication versions is insufficient.
cases.why_tricky: Both locators identify genuine papers in different volumes; a successful direct URL lookup can hide the secondary locator.

cases.independent_expected_behavior: Flag the mutually contradictory standard venue fields; do not call the entire citation Correct merely because journal wins field precedence.
cases.why_tricky: Both journal and booktitle are standard BibTeX metadata; the canonical input collapses them with journal or booktitle before comparisons. Correct direct DOI and title make all retained fields match.

cases.independent_expected_behavior: Flag the conflict between venue fields, preserving the correct booktitle as evidence rather than inventing a NeurIPS-to-ACL correction.
cases.why_tricky: The reverse of the shadowed_booktitle control reveals that order/field precedence changes the verdict for equivalent contradictions.

cases.independent_expected_behavior: Retain preprint and accepted-publication records separately; request review rather than voting a 2022 or 2023 year into a correction.

coverage_limitations: The fixed source universe is intentionally small; an absent replay paper is not evidence about live search coverage.
A bibliography cannot encode timeout, cache corruption or concurrency state; those remain supporting regression scenarios.
The key controls test cache containment and server-side literal-data round trips. DOM rendering safety is separately inspected in the viewer source; the evaluator does not execute a browser.

run_command.command: PYTHONPATH=src uv run --group dev python -m evaluation.adversarial --output ../../.local/bib-lint-adversarial
run_command.exit_status: 1 means a challenge expectation remains unmet; a completed audit can still fail the challenge.

scope_note: Scope-boundary classifications record the original challenge design; all listed desired behaviors are now mandatory regression checks.
